chunks: Whenever one of you greets, let him be loud with his greeting. He should not say, 'I greeted but they did not respond to me', for perhaps he greeted but they did not hear it. So whenever one of you responds, let him be loud with his response, and the one greeting should not say, 'I greeted but they did not respond to me'.

Then he said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Neither get angry nor anger others. Spread the greeting (salam) openly, make your speech pleasant, and pray at night while the people are sleeping — you will enter Paradise in safety'.
Then he (peace be upon him) recited to them the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'the Giver of Peace (Al-Salam), the Granter of Security (Al-Mu'min), the Guardian (Al-Muhaymin)' [59:23].

key_terms.أَفْشُوا السَّلَام: Spread/disseminate the greeting — a command to actively offer peace to others
key_terms.السَّلَام: The greeting of peace (Assalamu alaykum); also a Divine Name meaning the Source of Peace
key_terms.تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّة بِسَلَام: You will enter Paradise in safety — reward promised for the five practices

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about giving and responding to the Islamic greeting (salam)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs his companions on the proper etiquette of the Islamic greeting (salam): it must be spoken audibly so misunderstandings are avoided. He then transmits a teaching from Imam Ali (AS) — a five-part exhortation to avoid anger, spread peace, speak kindly, pray at night, and thereby earn entry into Paradise. The hadith concludes by anchoring these teachings in a divine attribute: God Himself is Al-Salam (the Source of Peace), establishing the theological grounding for making peace a central value of Muslim social life.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever one of you greets (السَّلَامُ), so let him be loud with his greeting. He should not be saying, ‘I greeted but he did not respond to me’, and perhaps he may have greeted and he did not hear it. So whenever one of you responds, so let him be loud with his response, and the one greeting one should not be saying, ‘I greeted, but he did not respond to me’.

Then heasws said: ‘It was so that Aliasws was saying: ‘Neither get angry nor anger (others). Openly offer the greetings (loudly) and be nice with your speech, and pray Salāt at nights while the people are sleeping, you would be entering the Paradise in safety’.
Then heasws recited the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [59:23] the Giver of peace, the Granter of security, Guardian over all’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al- Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “When anyone of you offers the greeting of peace he should say it loud and clear so he will not complain that no one answered his greeting of peace. He may have offered, but no one may have heard it and when any one of you answers the greeting he should say it loud and clear so that the one offering it will not say, ‘I offered them the greeting of peace but no one answered.’ “

The Imam then said, ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘If you do not become angry you will not be made angry, offer the greeting of peace loud and openly, speak nicely, perform prayer at night when people are sleeping and you will enter paradise in peace.’
Then he read the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy: ‘. . . the Peace, the Protector, the Watchful Guardian. . . .’” ( 59 : 23 )
